Implement training-only whole-item dropout on lookup activations: `e = item_emb(sequence) * sqrt(d)`; draw `keep = torch.rand((B,L,1), device=e.device, generator=aug_gen) >= p`; apply `e = e * keep.to(e.dtype) / (1-p)` for `0<p<1`. Broadcast across embedding dimensions, then add positional embeddings and execute existing ordinary dropout. Preserve padding masks derived from the original sequence IDs, positional indexing, padding-zeroing operations, causal masks, and target/loss masks exactly. Dropped real items remain valid positions; replacing IDs with padding would change the intervention. Disable augmentation during evaluation. This implementation follows the embedding/position ordering in [SASRec](https://github.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/blob/master/python/model.py) and inverted scaling in [PyTorch Dropout](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.dropout.Dropout.html).

Architectural implications: a zeroed item lookup still receives positional information. LayerNorm maps an entirely zero vector to its learned bias; attention, affine biases, and residual branches can produce nonzero states. Residuals preserve their actual branch input, so masking must precede any branch carrying the original item embedding. LayerNorm approximately cancels uniform positive scaling of its entire input, but scaling only the item component before positional addition changes their relative contribution. With tied input/output embeddings, mask lookup activations without modifying embedding weights or candidate embeddings: output-side gradients still update dropped items. These follow from [LayerNorm’s formula](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.modules.normalization.LayerNorm.html) and SASRec’s scoring code.

Create a persistent, separately seeded, device-compatible augmentation `torch.Generator`; checkpoint its `get_state()` and restore with `set_state()`. Explicit-generator draws leave default RNG streams untouched, preserving ordinary-dropout randomness when execution order/shapes match. Also isolate sampling/shuffling, match initialization, and restore all RNG states when resuming. Separate generators alone do not guarantee deterministic kernels or cross-platform reproducibility. [Generator](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.Generator.html), [reproducibility](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/notes/randomness.html).
